To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We introduce Leap, a novel framework for transfer learning that transfers knowledge across learning processes and outperforms competing transfer learning methods.

(i) we introduce a new transfer learning framework that transfers knowledge across learning processes; (ii) we show that this framework is able to outperform competing methods, both at meta-learning and transfer-learning tasks; and (iii) we demonstrate that Leap is able to transfer knowledge across learning process in reinforcement learning, where the number of gradient steps is in the order of millions.
we present a new framework for transfer learning, called Leap, that outperforms existing methods in a variety of scenarios.

the question: How can knowledge be transferred across learning processes?
the question of how to transfer knowledge across learning tasks.
the problem of learning how to learn, and in particular with learning how to learn from a few samples.

Leap is a framework that transfers knowledge across learning processes and achieves state-of-the-art results in a variety of settings, including meta-learning, transfer learning and reinforcement learning.

our approach is able to transfer knowledge across learning process in complex scenarios.

we propose an approach for transfer learning that transfers knowledge across learning processes, and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on computer vision and reinforcement learning tasks.

transfer learning at a higher level of abstraction can be achieved by transferring information contained in the manifold traversed during training.
